judgments.reasoning_cat1: The conversion block bundles several unfilled elections (plan, amount, date of new policy, retain/cancel balance of term insurance) with a beneficiary election that is either 'same as original policy' or 'per designation Form 3116 attached', so which beneficiary designation governs a converted policy is left genuinely open on the face of the form. The checkbox/blank structure means the operative terms depend on marks that the text itself does not resolve.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with the assignment question (c003), the paid-up change (c011) and the ratification/no-change carve-out (c019), which says amount, plan or benefits cannot change without written agreement; a conversion that alters plan and amount sits uneasily against that carve-out. Still, no direct contradiction is spelled out, so the risk is moderate rather than clear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple election of premium mode with dollar blanks and a cross-reference to 'CMAPP Section 03' for complete requirements; nothing in it carries two reasonable meanings once a box is checked. The 'Other' line is open-ended but is a fill-in, not an ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The only outside reference is to a separate procedures manual section, not to another provision of this form; nothing in the loan, withdrawal or endorsement provisions contradicts it. Low relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A binary yes/no question with a conditional instruction to submit new assignment forms; the only softness is 'appropriate' forms, which is procedural rather than meaning-changing. Little for a court to construe in the words themselves.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with the loan request's assignment of 'all right, title and interest' as security (c005) and with the 'ASSIGNEE'S CONSENT IS GIVEN TO THIS CHANGE' signature block, but those can be harmonised as different kinds of assignment. No genuine conflict identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare heading with a checkbox and no stated terms, amount, date or conditions for the guaranteed purchase option, so its content is entirely outside the provision. Incompleteness of this kind gives little to construe but also states nothing definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The option's substance would have to come from the underlying policy rider, and nothing else on this form addresses it; no inconsistency with the conversion, loan or endorsement provisions appears. Low relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The cash/gross loan mechanics ('on full or gross loans, policy loan interest is deducted while loan interest is added to any net loan') are confusingly expressed, and the 'Occasion' list (Marriage, Birth or Adoption) with an open 'Occasion' blank raises a list-scope question. It also assigns 'all right, title and interest' in the policy as 'sole security', a broad phrase against a security-limited purpose.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The security assignment must be squared with the separate assignment question (c003) and the assignee-consent block, and with the release provision (c020) on cancellation of part of the policy. Those can be harmonised, so the relational risk is real but modest.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision reads 'Change basic amount from $252000 to $___' with the destination amount left blank, so the single operative figure of the change is missing from the text itself — a mechanical defect that determines what coverage the policy carries. This is the one substantively filled election on the form, making the blank the natural focus of a dispute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits directly against c019's statement that 'there can be no change [in] amount ... unless I agree to it in writing' and against the Home Office Endorsement block effective December 1995, so whether a basic-amount change took effect turns on reading those together. That is a concrete relational tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Change from type ___ to type ___' with both blanks empty; the word 'type' is undefined on the form, but there is no filled content to fight over. Minimal intrinsic content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Related to the conversion provision (c001), which also speaks of rider 'type', but nothing contradicts it elsewhere in the instrument. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard replacement-disclosure question asking whether additional insurance applied for is intended to replace, 'in whole or in part', any existing insurance or annuities; 'intended to replace' is somewhat elastic but is a regulatory formula. The follow-up instruction to give company name and policy number is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing in the conversion, paid-up or endorsement provisions bears on it; it is a disclosure, not an operative promise. Low relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fragmentary net/gross withdrawal election — '(Amount of check)' versus 'Gross (amount of withdrawal including charges)' — which is a definitional label rather than a promise, though 'charges' is undefined here. Little independent meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels the net/gross language of the loan request (c005) and is consistent with it; no conflict located elsewhere. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain instruction to check box A to decline federal withholding and box B to have withholding apply; the meaning of each box is stated. Nothing ambiguous once read with the boxes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Must be read with c014, c016 and the 20% withholding note at c017, and those fit together as election plus consequence rather than conflicting. Low.
